clue.text: Pedestrian coming in our direction?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dull, unimaginative, lacking any lift
second meaning, read literally: heading towards this planet we live on

explanation.surface: Someone on foot is walking straight towards us.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: something heading for our planet is literally bound for Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian, prosaic mind is said to be earthbound, unable to soar imaginatively above ordinary things.

clue.text: Burning a mark on trunk

parts.note: taken as written
a blaze is a mark cut into the bark of a tree to show a trail

explanation.surface: Someone is branding or scorching a sign onto a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire is in flames, so the adjective describing a fiercely flaming thing fits here.

clue.text: To set up enclosure, church needed small contribution

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to put something is to set it down
a pen is an enclosure for animals
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Building a church fence required only a modest donation.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuppence, two old British pennies, is the classic small sum; 'To set' must be read as one verb before going upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuppence, two pence, stands for any trivial sum, as in giving your tuppence worth to a discussion.

clue.text: Link road in West End

parts.note: a bond is a tie or connection
a street is a town road

explanation.surface: A connecting road in London's theatre and shopping district.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines while its first two words build the answer. Bond Street is an upmarket shopping street in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond Street is a famous thoroughfare in central London's West End, renowned for luxury shops and galleries.

clue.text: Without any qualifications, say? Lady takes no notice

parts.note: to utter is to say

indicators.note: taking no part of something means removing those letters from the word

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A woman with no formal qualifications ignores what she is told.
explanation.walkthrough: LADY loses AD to leave LY, appended to UTTER. The question mark hints that 'say' is wordplay rather than an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly means completely, absolutely, with no reservations or hedging attached to the statement.

clue.text: There's no sin in doctor using this

definitions.text: There's no sin in doctor using this

parts.note: Dr is the standard abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: 'no' says the following letters are absent, so they are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is no wrongdoing for a physician to prescribe this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a doctor may prescribe it without any wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug is a medicine, the sort of thing a physician legitimately prescribes and administers to patients.

clue.text: Supercilious member of parliamentary opposition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: offhand, haughty and dismissive
second meaning: a Royalist who fought against the Parliamentarians

explanation.surface: An arrogant opposition MP.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a modern opposition backbencher, but the opposition meant is to Parliament itself, in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is arrogantly offhand; Cavaliers were King Charles I's supporters fighting the Roundheads.

clue.text: End of fighting in Europe for part of army

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it

parts.note: Britons call mainland Europe the Continent

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of fighting

explanation.surface: When war ends in Europe, a body of troops is sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside CONTINENT, between the N and the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a detachment of troops, a group forming one section of a larger military force.

clue.text: Instruction to players — run about all over the place

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: something scattered all over the place is out of its proper order

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Telling sportsmen to dash around everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests a team on a pitch; they are musicians. 'Run about' looks like one phrase, but only 'about' is mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is a musical direction telling performers to vary the tempo freely for expressive effect.

clue.text: Fastening that comes undone is a problem on undergarment

parts.note: a slip is a woman's undergarment, a petticoat
a knot is a tricky problem, as in a knotty question

explanation.surface: A fastening that keeps coming undone on one's underwear is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'on' means placed after: the problem follows the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipknot is a knot designed to untie easily with a pull, or to slide along its rope.

clue.text: Urge factory to produce fruit

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
a plant is an industrial factory

explanation.surface: Pressing a factory to grow produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the aubergine is a berry, and Americans call this vegetable-like fruit by this name.

clue.text: Pronouncement of writer and statesman

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a writer

explanation.surface: A statement issued by an author who is also a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: William Penn was the Quaker statesman who founded Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: William Penn, colonial founder of Pennsylvania, was an English Quaker leader and statesman of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Head of local order almost showing non-cleric up

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: proving is showing to be true

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: laic means a layman, someone not in holy orders

explanation.surface: A local religious leader is almost exposed by a layperson.
explanation.walkthrough: PROVING loses its G, and LAIC goes upwards to CIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic religious orders, a provincial is the superior governing all houses within one province.

clue.text: Alternative medium for novelist, i.e. after adaptation

indicators.note: an adaptation reshapes material into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's book gets adapted for the small screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a novel being adapted for broadcasting, which is exactly where the answer sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Television is a broadcast medium, an alternative to print for telling a story to an audience.

clue.text: Novel event in Pilgrim's Progress

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Thackeray's book about Becky Sharp
second meaning: the year-round market in Bunyan's town of Vanity

explanation.surface: A new occurrence in Bunyan's allegory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray took the title of his satirical novel from Bunyan's fair, a worldly marketplace Christian passes through.

clue.text: Soldiers without officers run into action, as commanded

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: running into something puts one thing inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Leaderless troops charge into battle as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers without officers' means the other ranks, not soldiers missing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done as ordered is done as commanded, in accordance with instructions given.

clue.text: Joint vote arranged in foreign parliament

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside it
arranged means put into a fresh order

parts.note: the word vote, with its letters rearranged
the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A coalition ballot is organised in an overseas legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint vote' reads as one phrase, but 'Joint' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a carpentry joint of interlocking wedge-shaped tenons, often used in drawers.

clue.text: Grenade's exploding — defend yourself!

indicators.note: an explosion blows something apart so the pieces land in a new order

parts.note: the word itself, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A warning shout as a bomb goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining fodder to indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call warning an opponent to take a guarded stance, ready to parry.

clue.text: Such quaint charm is a thing of the past

definitions.text: Such quaint charm is a thing of the past

indicators.note: quaint suggests something oddly put together, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Old-world charm of this kind belongs to a bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a definition too: quaint old charm is something out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an old-fashioned word, style or custom surviving from an earlier period.

clue.text: Philosopher's inclination to act badly

parts.note: a bent is a natural tendency
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: A thinker's tendency towards misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act badly' suggests misbehaving, but it means acting in the theatrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham was the English philosopher who founded utilitarianism, seeking the greatest happiness for most people.

clue.text: Suitably dressed for service in siege

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: wearing the robe a priest wears to take a church service
second meaning: surrounding a place with troops

explanation.surface: Someone properly attired for duty during a siege.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into IN VESTMENT; a vestment is a clergyman's ceremonial robe.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is an old military term for besieging it, so the noun means a blockade.

clue.text: Rabbit caught by bowler, say

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a bowler is a kind of hat, a derby

explanation.surface: A batsman who is a poor player is caught out by the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket slang a rabbit is a hopeless batsman, which suits the surface. In British slang to rabbit is to talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk, means to chatter at length.

clue.text: Defensive formation a club is assembling

parts.note: taken as written
a bat is a club used in games
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports team is setting up its back line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembling' tempts an anagram of 'a club is', but the letters do not fit; the pieces are simply put together.
explanation.definitionFit: An abatis is a barricade of felled trees with sharpened branches pointing towards an attacking enemy.

clue.text: Eye problem can make one fall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clouding of the lens of the eye

explanation.surface: Poor eyesight can cause someone to trip over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' reads as a stumble; it is a noun, a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an opacity of the eye's lens and a great waterfall or torrent.

clue.text: Boy that's raised in France

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means lifted so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: cela is French for that
not letters: tells you to translate the word before into French

explanation.surface: A lad brought up in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised in France' looks like a boy's upbringing; 'in France' tells you to translate 'that' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec, short for Alexander, is a common masculine first name, so it stands for any boy.

clue.text: Gemstone for flower-girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reddish-orange variety of zircon
second meaning: a spring bulb flower that is also a girl's name

explanation.surface: A jewel given to a bridesmaid.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower girl is a young bridesmaid; here the hyphenated phrase means a girl's name that is also a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyacinth is a gem, a fragrant spring bulb with dense flower spikes, and a woman's first name.

clue.text: Each bird caught by expert is possibly a rook

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: Every bird snared by a skilled hunter might be a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is 'a piece', and a rook is a chess piece; the bird surface hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in costing a pound apiece; a chessman such as the rook is a piece.

clue.text: Include with award in negotiated settlement

indicators.note: a word holding another with it inside carries it in its middle

parts.note: to comprise is to include
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An agreement is reached that adds a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour limited to a small number of members.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is an agreement reached by each side conceding something during bargaining.
